paragraphs: The next round of proposals came in the late 1790s. Charles Willson Peale, the noted painter, started publishing articles in the local newspapers in 1796 about a 390-foot single span bridge he designed and asked the Select Council to view his model. He was issued a patent on January 21, 1797, for a bridge he indicated would fit the Market Street site and followed it up with a pamphlet of 16 pages entitled An Essay on Building Wooden Bridges describing his patent for a laminated wood arch. His arch was built up of 1-inch thick plank laid on the flat with overlapping sides, and the planks butted to one another with the entire wooden deck pegged with hemlock trunnels.

recorded.title: STRUCTURE magazine | The Permanent Bridge
recorded.text:
Smith’s proposed covered bridge 1787.
The next round of proposals came in the late 1790s. Charles Willson Peale, the noted painter, started publishing articles in the local newspapers in 1796 about a 390-foot single span bridge he designed and asked the Select Council to view his model. He was issued a patent on January 21, 1797, for a bridge he indicated would fit the Market Street site and followed it up with a pamphlet of 16 pages entitled An Essay on Building Wooden Bridges describing his patent for a laminated wood arch. His arch was built up of 1-inch thick plank laid on the flat with overlapping sides, and the planks butted to one another with the entire wooden deck pegged with hemlock trunnels.
Peale’s Bridge.
